title: How Lenny Rachitsky built a $500K+/year newsletter: quality, time and primary research
summary: Lenny explains how he grew his newsletter and podcast with no hacks: consistent high-quality content, lots of time, and primary research rooted in real audience problems. He also covers early growth sources, Substack recommendations, ruthless editing, and the downsides of the creator treadmill.

principles.text: Sustainable content growth comes from consistency and quality, not hacks; referrals and paid ads barely moved the trend line.
principles.quote: nothing helps it grow other than just consistency and quality of content.

principles.text: Root content in a real problem someone has. Starting as an advice column kept the work grounded in actual needs.
principles.quote: that content is rooted in a real problem somebody actually has, not just me pontificating on something that may be a thing.

principles.text: Pick the job your content does for the reader, then do that job better than anyone else.
principles.quote: figure out what's the job you're doing for someone, and then just do that better than anyone else that's doing it out there.

principles.text: Do primary research on behalf of your audience (talk to the companies directly); it delivers expensive-to-get value cheaply.
principles.quote: I'm just doing primary research on behalf of people, and it's like very low cost for them.

principles.text: Time invested drives quality. Going full-time and spending many more hours per piece is the edge.
principles.quote: I find a really direct correlation between the amount of time I put into something and the success of that piece.

principles.text: Build the newsletter first, then launch a podcast. Sharing each episode with an existing audience makes podcast growth easier.
principles.quote: build an awesome newsletter and then launch a podcast. It's harder, I think, the other way around.
